intro: On Bülbüldağı, in İzmir province, stands a stone house held to be where Mary spent her last years. This is the House of the Virgin Mary, a monastery and church whose foundations date to the 1st century AD. Popes have visited it, and it is a place of pilgrimage for Christians and Muslims alike.
history: The stone house on the slope of Bülbüldağı was sought out on the strength of the visions of a German nun, Anne Catherine Emmerich, and it was found in 1891. Its foundations date to the first century AD, and part of its walls to the Byzantine period. Popes Paul VI, John Paul II and Benedict XVI have all come here.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the stone house, the wishing wall, the water springs and the chapel.
facts: Did you know? This is one of the few places of pilgrimage visited by Christians and Muslims alike: Mary is the only woman named in the Qur'an. And the house itself was found in 1891, sought out on the strength of a German nun's visions.
outro: This brings our journey through the House of the Virgin Mary to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
